data.name: authority
data.source: searchParams — since `a-lost-authority-is-not-a-refusal`, the sentence a performDeploy whose account authority is gone redirected back with. Read before anything else and, when present, it replaces the whole page with <AuthorityLost>. It is not a refusal of this deployment and does not travel as ?problem=.

components.purpose: Two steps on one route: choose a market, then agree to what deploying there does — with the replacement named before anything is agreed to.
components.current_implementation: max-w-2xl centered column, space-y-4, p-6 — the confirmation-page skeleton. Branch order: not-connected, then authority-lost, then the roster read. Without ?coin&timeframe it is the chooser; with them the describe runs and the page becomes the confirmation. chooser-no-timeframes replaces the form with a role=alert sentence. refused renders h1 'Cannot deploy' + the reason (role=alert, untinted text) + an underlined 'Choose differently' link. no-such-agent and roster-unreadable are the shared refusal skeletons with underlined links. Since `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` all five describe-reaching branches mount `<CarriedProblem>` unconditionally as the first thing under the h1 — it renders null when there is no carried reason, so every `-with-problem` pairing above is a real rendering rather than a variant somebody has to remember. Note what the pairings mean visually: on refused and roster-unreadable two alerts stack — the carried reason for the click that bounced, then this page's own fresh failure — and they are two different facts about two different moments. NEW since `a-lost-authority-is-not-a-refusal`: `authority-lost` is a sixth top-level branch, taken before the roster is even read, that returns the shared `<AuthorityLost>` and nothing else — no chooser, no proposal, no form, and deliberately no CarriedProblem even when a ?problem= rode in alongside.
constraints: The page renders whole from one server round trip — no client JS, no hydration. A design requiring client-side interactivity changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

The two steps must stay two requests: the chooser's GET composes a description and reaches no operation; only the confirm form performs — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:40-41 ('SHALL perform it only after a person confirms against the specific agent and market').

Every describe-reaching branch renders the carried reason, not just the ones that can offer a form — the branch that drops it loses the only record of what the click did, and `tests/agent/refusals-reach-the-operator.test.ts` asserts one `<CarriedProblem>` per `<main>` in this file. A design that suppresses it on a terminal branch changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

Where two alerts stack (carried reason above this page's own failure reason), both must stay readable as separate claims — collapsing them into one block would merge 'your deploy was refused' with 'the roster would not load'.

The authority-lost branch renders no form and no carried problem, on purpose — 'a control that cannot work is not made honest by the sentence above it' (authority-lost.tsx). A design that gives this branch the chooser back, or dresses it as one more refusal beside the others, changes behavior and is requires-spec-change.

components.purpose: Name the market to deploy to.
components.current_implementation: A required free-text input (placeholder 'HYPE') wearing the shared CONTROL constant under a LABEL, inside the chooser's method=get form. No coin list is offered — a mistyped coin only surfaces after the round trip, as the describe's refusal.
constraints: Field styling goes through the CONTROL/LABEL constants in control.ts, not a per-page className.
Offering a picked list instead of free text would change behavior (a new data read) — requires-spec-change.

components.purpose: Pick a timeframe from the ones BattleGrid currently declares.
components.current_implementation: A select wearing CONTROL under a LABEL, options mapped straight from the runtime declaration.
constraints: The options MUST come from the platform's own declaration discovered at runtime, never a list compiled into the product — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:41-43 and :70-74. A design must not hard-code or reorder them into a curated set.

components.purpose: Show the refusal that bounced a submitted deploy back to the person who clicked it — on whichever branch the page then lands.
components.current_implementation: The shared `CarriedProblem` component (src/presentation/components/carried-problem.tsx), extracted by `the-outcome-reaches-the-person` from the ternary that used to be inline on this page. Carries DT-0004's danger treatment unchanged — rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert, opening with a semibold 'Refused: ' prefix so the state is named as well as tinted — and returns null when `problem` is undefined, which is what lets every branch mount it unconditionally.
constraints: role=alert must survive.

The reason shown is the one the platform returned, on the surface acted from — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:76-79. Do not truncate or paraphrase; the string is platform-authored and unbounded, so the block must wrap rather than clip.

Shared by eleven pages now (agent deploy/undeploy/rebind/archive/reactivate, strategy archive/restore/fork, both /pending surfaces, recorder trim) — restyle it in the component, never per page, or the renderings of one paragraph drift the way they did before it was extracted. `tests/agent/refusals-reach-the-operator.test.ts` fails any file that hand-rolls it again.
Rendering nothing when there is no problem is load-bearing — a design must not give it a reserved empty slot or a placeholder.
The 'Refused: ' prefix is part of the treatment — a design may restyle the prefix but must not drop the naming of the state.
This is a failed attempt, not advisory — 'notice never borrows danger's colour' (system.json principle) binds the consequence block beside it.

components.purpose: State what deploying does — including whose deployment is replaced if the market is occupied — in the sentence the token was issued against, before the button.
components.current_implementation: rounded-gc-2 border border-consequence-border bg-consequence-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary with role=alert. DT-0016 has landed: the anonymous border-border-default this was built with is gone and the block now wears the house consequence role, the same one the strategy archive callout and the recorder-trim description already wore.
constraints: The text is the string stored with the confirmation token — a design must not paraphrase, truncate, or summarize it.

Where the market is occupied the sentence names who is replaced, before agreement — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:45-47 ('the confirmation MUST say whose deployment is replaced, before agreement'). It must not be de-emphasised below the buttons.
Consequence outranks everything on a screen (system.json principle).
role=alert must survive.

components.purpose: Ask what deploying to a named market would do, and offer the way back — the step before anything is agreed to.

actions.effect: GET-navigates to the same route carrying the coin and timeframe, which puts the page into its proposal branch. Composes a description and reaches no operation.

components.current_implementation: A plain `flex flex-wrap gap-3` div inside the chooser's `method="get"` form, holding a BUTTON_SECONDARY submit ('See what deploying would do') and a BUTTON_SECONDARY anchor ('Back to the agent'). Both controls are secondary by control.ts's stated rule — this form asks and reaches no operation, so the weight is kept for the page that follows. **It never received DT-0016's mobile treatment**, so it is still a wrapping row while `perform-deploy` one branch along is a full-width stack under `tablet`.
constraints: Both controls stay secondary. This form composes a description and reaches no operation; promoting the submit to primary would say the page commits something, and the weight belongs to the proposal branch that follows.

The submit must stay a GET submit, not a server action. `reachability.test.ts` leans on that distinction in six places, and `confirmation-is-human.test.ts` exists because a describe and its perform were once the same request.
The row is inside the form; the field labels above it are not part of it. A design must not restack the fields to suit the row.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle), in both layouts.
This row and `perform-deploy` are two rows on one route that a user meets one after the other. They should not disagree about what a confirmation row looks like.

components.purpose: Carry the deploy decision: one committing button, one visible way out.

actions.effect: POSTs the server action with agentId, coinId, timeframe, expectedRevision, confirmationToken; success lands on /agents/[id], refusal redirects back here with coin, timeframe and ?problem= preserved so the describe re-runs; a lost account authority redirects back with ?authority= alone — no coin, no timeframe — which renders the page as AuthorityLost with no form

components.current_implementation: flex flex-col gap-3 tablet:flex-row tablet:flex-wrap — DT-0016 has landed: the row stacks full-width below the `tablet` breakpoint and only becomes a wrapping row above it, matching the archive page. Five hidden inputs carry the confirmation binding, with expectedRevision serialized as '' when null (a first deployment).
constraints: The hidden binding is the confirmation ceremony — the form must keep exactly one submit path.

The stacking breakpoint is `tablet`; both controls carry `w-full tablet:w-auto` so the commit and its peer are the same width when stacked. A design must not restore a wrapping row at mobile width, which is what put the cancel on its own line under a full-width commit.
expectedRevision: null is the platform's documented first-deploy signal — openspec/specs/agent-deployment/spec.md:49-56 — and must keep riding the form untouched.
Cancel must remain a visible peer of the submit, never a text link beneath it (DT-0002 ruling, restated in control.ts).

components.current_implementation: BUTTON_PRIMARY constant from control.ts — accent.default bg, min-h-control (44px, DT-0003's token), rounded-gc-2, hover to accent.hover over duration-fast, active holds hover at duration-instant. Since DT-0016 it carries `w-full tablet:w-auto` on the confirmation branch, so it fills the stacked row on mobile. No pending/loading state between click and redirect. system.json declares this primitive with states [default, hover, active, focused, disabled, loading]; `disabled` and `loading` are declared there as names with no treatment and are implemented by nothing in control.ts, so no form in the product can reach them (#153). The harness half of that is now solved — tests/rendering/support/form-status.ts reaches both states — so what is missing is the look, which is this round's to decide. DT-0022 added the primitive's `disabled` treatment to this constant — bg.sunken ground, text.disabled label, border.subtle edge and cursor not-allowed, stated rather than an opacity. DT-0022 defined the primitive's `disabled` treatment on this constant, but **nothing in the product enters it** — so it is not listed as a state of this surface. system.json declares it and DT-0022 styles it; a surface claiming a state it cannot reach is the same fiction DT-0003 refused for the ghost and danger variants.
constraints: Deliberately NOT danger-styled — DT-0002's ruling, restated in control.ts: the weight belongs on the consequence block naming the replacement.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_PRIMARY constant in control.ts, shared by every committing submit in the product.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).
Focus ring comes from the one global rule in globals.css — do not add a per-element ring.

components.purpose: In the chooser: the ask ('See what deploying would do') and the way back. In the confirmation: 'Leave things as they are'.

actions.effect: The chooser submit GET-navigates into the describe; the anchors return to /agents/[id] without submitting anything

components.current_implementation: BUTTON_SECONDARY constant from control.ts — inline-flex centering, min-h-control, bordered, DT-0004's hover (border-strong + bg-sunken). Worn here by the chooser's GET submit (secondary because it only asks — control.ts's stated rule) and by the chooser's 'Back to the agent' anchor and the confirmation's cancel; the cancel additionally carries `w-full tablet:w-auto` since DT-0016. The chooser's own row is modelled as `deploy-chooser-row` since 2026-08-13 — it was prose here before, which is why DT-0016 could not reach it. The refused, roster-unreadable and no-such-agent branches still use plain underlined prose links rather than this treatment. Where this is an anchor it can never be pending — it submits nothing. Where a surface uses it as a GET submit (the deploy chooser's ask), it can, and system.json's declared `disabled` and `loading` states are unimplemented there too (#153). Recorded on button-primary rather than here, because that is the control a perform runs through.
constraints: The cancel must remain an anchor (pure navigation, no form participation) and a visible peer of the submit.
The chooser's submit must stay secondary — it composes a description and reaches no operation; promoting it to primary misstates what it does.
Styling changes go through the BUTTON_SECONDARY constant in control.ts.
44px minimum tap target (system.json principle).

components.purpose: Tell an operator whose agent did not load whether to wait or to reconnect — and that their agent is not gone.
components.current_implementation: Shared WhyNotLoaded (why-not-loaded.tsx), a plain mt-2 paragraph under the 'Could not load this agent' heading. Two sentences, chosen by cause carried out of the read itself.
constraints: The refused/unreachable distinction must stay two different sentences — a platform that answered and declined is not one that could not be reached (agent-authoring's reasoning, shared by this component product-wide).

components.purpose: Say that the account's BattleGrid authority is gone — not that this deployment was refused — where the operator was standing when their submit failed.

actions.effect: Anchor to /connect, where a new grant is obtained. Rendered only on remedy-reconnect. It navigates and submits nothing, and it is not the operation that failed — that control stays absent on both branches.

components.current_implementation:
Shared `AuthorityLost` component (src/presentation/components/authority-lost.tsx), also mounted by the agent deploy, undeploy and rebind pages and the strategy rule editor. It replaces the whole page rather than banding the top of one: its own `
`, h1 'Your BattleGrid authority is no longer valid' in text-text-primary, the carried sentence in `rounded-gc-2 border border-danger-default bg-danger-subtle p-4 text-sm text-text-primary` with role=alert — the same treatment CarriedProblem wears — then a text-sm text-text-secondary paragraph: 'Nothing was changed. Until this is fixed, no operation on this account can succeed — including the one you just tried.' **Since `a-remedy-is-a-target-not-a-sentence` (#182) it also takes the deployment's `remedy` and branches on it.** On `reconnect` it appends a `

` holding a BUTTON_SECONDARY anchor to /connect reading 'Connect your BattleGrid account again'. On `repair-the-key` it appends nothing, because replacing an environment variable and restarting a process is not something a link can do. The remedy value is fixed once at src/composition.ts (`config.personal ? 'repair-the-key' : 'reconnect'`) and passed down, so the component never works out which deployment it is on. Nothing has designed any of this; it was built wearing existing tokens, and the anchor reuses the primitive NotConnected already uses for the same purpose rather than introducing a treatment.
constraints: It renders instead of the ceremony, not above it — a design must not turn this into a banner over the chooser or the proposal. The reason the page has no form is that no call on this account can succeed.

The sentence is passed in and printed verbatim, remedy included — a design must not template it or prefix it. The remedy is **also offered as a target where the deployment has one**: the component links to /connect on `remedy-reconnect` and draws nothing on `remedy-repair-the-key`. A design must not draw that link unconditionally — that is how a personal deployment gets told to press a connect button it does not have — and must not remove it from the reconnect branch, where DT-0006's ruling holds: a remedy is a target, not a sentence.

The two branches are one component and one treatment. The difference between them is whether the anchor renders, not how the page looks. A design that gave the two deployments different layouts would be designing for a distinction the operator can neither see nor change.

It must stay visually distinct from CarriedProblem even though both currently wear danger: one says this attempt was refused and something else may work, the other says nothing will. If a design keeps them identical it should say that is a decision.
role=alert must survive on the reason.
Shared with agent undeploy, agent rebind and the strategy rule editor — restyle it in the component, never per page.

components.purpose: Turn away a request without authority, with the one remedy that works: connect.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, and since DT-0006 the connect link is an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — the way in as a target, not a sentence, at the 44px floor with secondary's hover. Used by every authenticated page, so this treatment is inherited everywhere. This is the one branch that does not mount CarriedProblem — it renders before searchParams are read.
constraints: Every no-authority cause renders this same page by design (see design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants.

flows.name: Deploy an agent to a market
steps: arrive from the agent page
name a coin and pick a declared timeframe
submit 'See what deploying would do' — a GET that composes the describe
read the consequence, including who is replaced if the market is occupied
submit 'Deploy <name>'
land on /agents/[id] with the deployment made

flows.name: The deploy is refused after submit
steps: submit
platform refuses (revision moved, not permitted)
redirected back with coin, timeframe and ?problem= preserved
the describe re-runs and the problem banner (shared CarriedProblem) states the reason above the fresh proposal

flows.name: The bounce lands on a branch that fails too
steps: submit; the platform refuses and redirects back with ?problem=
the re-describe also refuses, or the roster will not load
the problem banner (shared CarriedProblem) still states why the click was refused, above the fresh reason for this branch — both facts, not one

flows.name: The account's authority is gone
steps: submit 'Deploy <name>'
the platform answers that the connection or credential is no longer valid
performDeploy's authority-lost arm redirects back here with ?authority= — not ?problem=, and without the coin and timeframe
the page renders <AuthorityLost> alone: the reason, and that nothing was changed and nothing on this account can succeed until it is fixed. No form to retry with.

flows.name: Nothing can be composed
steps: BattleGrid declares no timeframes, or the describe refuses the chosen market
the page says so and offers 'Choose differently' or nothing to submit

flows.name: Walk away
steps: click 'Leave things as they are'
back on /agents/[id], nothing changed

accessibility.notes: The carried problem, consequence, no-timeframes, refusal and authority-lost messages all carry role=alert; on a bounced branch two of them are adjacent. The authority-lost branch has an alert and no focusable element at all — it is the one state on this surface with nothing to tab to. Focus ring is global (focus-visible, 2px). No client JS: every state change is a full navigation.
